01-introduction.html
2 Case Study

2 Case Study In the following examples, we will be using a random selection of hospitals from the Open Database of Hospital Facilities in Canada. Hospitals frequently house at-risk populations of individuals, and are an interesting point to make a case study demonstrating this workflow. We are imagining that the hospital administration delivered a survey to all employees that had worked at each location for a minimum of two years. This data is then being analyzed by us, to determine the impact of environmental exposures in the past two years.

3 Wildfires 3.1 Environmental Data Preparation 3.2 Compute Intersections 3.3 Date Lag 3.4 Binary Matrix 3.5 Map

3 Wildfires Wildfires can have strong impacts on an environment that are disproportionate to the footprint size of the fires themselves. Smoke from fires has been recorded to stretch thousands of kilometres #REF#. Wildfires are widely studied in environmental exposure impact analysis… 3.1 Environmental Data Preparation Data can be downloaded for free from the Canadian Wildland Fire Information System. To begin with the wildfire data, we read the NBAC wildfire polygons (1972-2024) from the .shp file available from CWFIS. Tip: Shapefiles are a set of files. Ensure the .shp, .shx, .dbf, and (ideally) .prj sit together in the same folder. #read in the NBAC data poly_fires <- st_read(r"(./data/FireData/NBAC_1972to2024_20250506.shp)") #look at the data str(poly_fires) #normalise column names names(poly_fires) <- tolower(names(poly_fires)) #Given the extremely large size, it's best to reduce the dataset to include only the years required poly_fires <- poly_fires %>% filter(year >= 2015) #limit to a selection of columns that are relevant poly_fires <- select(poly_fires, nfireid, basrc, year, ag_sdate, #agency start date as date format ag_edate, #agency end date as date format poly_ha, admin_area, geometry) #rename columns for easier understanding poly_fires <- poly_fires %>% mutate( start_day = day(ag_sdate), start_month = month(ag_sdate), start_year = year(ag_sdate), end_day = day(ag_edate), end_month = month(ag_edate), end_year = year(ag_edate), start_date = ag_sdate, end_date = ag_edate, size = poly_ha) %>% select(-poly_ha) #remove the original poly_ha column #write the newly formed dataset to memory, it will be loaded and used in this example st_write_parquet(poly_fires, r"(./data/wildfire_data_sf.parquet)") names(poly_fires) 3.2 Compute Intersections Here, we load the hospital data for computing intersections. We are going to add a 25km buffer around each hospital to help identify fires with a perimeter that approached the hospitals. buffer_distance = 25000 #in metres #load hospital data odhf_data <- read.csv("./data/odhf_hospitals.csv", row.names = 1) # get ready to convert hospital data odhf_fires <- odhf_data %>% mutate(long = as.numeric(long)) %>% filter(!is.na(lat) & !is.na(long)) #filter out na points odhf_fires_sf <- odhf_fires %>% st_as_sf(coords=c("long", "lat"), crs = st_crs(4326)) #transform to a metres pcs odhf_fires_sf <- st_transform(odhf_fires_sf, st_crs(poly_fires)) #Create buffer around each location odhf_buffers <- st_buffer(odhf_fires_sf, dist = buffer_distance) #buffer in metres We need to compute the intersections between the fires and buffered hospitals. To streamline this example, we select only fires greater than 200 hectares for computing intersections using EPSG 3978. min_fire_size <- 200 #in ha #filter fires by size poly_fires <- poly_fires %>% filter(size > min_fire_size) #intersection matrix, the product refers to row indices, not id numbers fire_matches <- st_intersects(odhf_buffers, poly_fires) #run st_intersection to get geometries, but takes way longer Now that we have found the indexes of the intersections in fire_matches, we need to link this information back to the original, more detailed dataframe. #create the intersection dataframe from the intersection matrix intersection_df <- map2_dfr(seq_along(fire_matches), fire_matches, ~ tibble( hospital_id = odhf_fires_sf$hospital_id[.x], #.x indicates it's from the sequence (argument 1) n_fire_id = poly_fires$nfireid[.y], #.y indicates it's from the fires (argument 2) survey_year = odhf_fires_sf$survey_year[.x], survey_month = odhf_fires_sf$survey_month[.x], fire_start_date = poly_fires$ag_sdate[.y], fire_end_date = poly_fires$ag_edate[.y], geometry = poly_fires$geometry[.y], intersects = 1 ) ) #create useful date fields for the 24-month date lag intersection_df$survey_eom_date <- ymd(paste(intersection_df$survey_year, intersection_df$survey_month, "01", sep = "-")) + months(1) - days(1) intersection_df$survey_25_prev <- ymd(paste(intersection_df$survey_year, intersection_df$survey_month, "01", sep = "-")) -months(24) intersection_df$fire_start_date <- as.Date(intersection_df$fire_start_date, format="%YYYY-%MM-%DD")#make into a date intersection_df$fire_end_date <- as.Date(intersection_df$fire_end_date, format="%YYYY-%MM-%DD")#make into a date We also need to deal with extraneous cases like rows with no fire end dates and those that were recorded as instantaneous (same start and end date). #this gets all overlapping dates, treating rows with no fire end date as one day instantaneous events intersection_overlap <- intersection_df %>% mutate( #define effective fire range: point if no end date, range otherwise fire_start_eff = fire_start_date, fire_end_eff = coalesce(fire_end_date, fire_start_date) ) %>% filter( #survey range overlaps with fire range survey_25_prev <= fire_end_eff, survey_eom_date >= fire_start_eff ) 3.3 Date Lag As part of the exposure determination, we are interested in the 24 months prior to each survey date at the hospitals. Hospitals were surveyed at different times, so the date of the survey will be recorded along with each month from the 0th to 24th month prior (survey month, survey month - 1, survey month - 2, etc.). #expand each survey row into last 24 months expand_months <- function(d, hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year) { data.table( hospital_id = hospital_id, survey_year = survey_year, survey_month = survey_month, offset = 0:24, date = format(ceiling_date(d %m-% months(0:24), "month") - days(1), "%Y%m") ) } #apply the function #identifies how many months a given month is offset from the 0th month for that hospitals survey date odhf_fires_sf$dates <- ymd(paste(odhf_fires_sf$survey_year, odhf_fires_sf$survey_month, "01", sep = "-")) + months(1) - days(1) #for unique examples (one hospital-survey combo) fires_un <- unique(odhf_fires_sf, by = c("hospial_id","dates")) fires_un <- as.data.table(fires_un) survey_expanded <- fires_un[, expand_months(dates, hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year), by = .(hospital_id, dates)] #expand the months backwards for each unique hospital_id/date ## Processed 510 groups out of 1047. 49% done. months. #create a detailed data frame of all intersections and non-intersections, regardless of date, as an intermediary product fires_detailed <- survey_expanded %>% left_join(intersection_df, by = 4 Floods Floods are a common environmental hazard in Canada. Numerous flooding events have been reported in popular media and studied in literature… 4.1 Environmental Data Preparation Natural Resources Canada provides a flood archive data set through Open Canada. The data is provided in bulk as a .gdb file with several layers. We are specifically interested in the ‘EGS_Flood_Product_Archive’ layer. #load raw flood data gdb_path <- "./data/EGS_Flood_Product_Archive.gdb" st_layers(gdb_path) flood_data <- st_read(gdb_path, layer = "EGS_Flood_Product_Archive", options = "METHOD=SKIP") 4.2 Data Preparation Before any analysis can proceed with the flood data, the hospital data needs to be loaded and converted to an appropriate coordinate reference system that aligns with the flood data. #load the hospital data odhf_data <- read.csv("./data/odhf_hospitals.csv", row.names = 1) #need to make some data to verify #names throw an error due to character incompatibility, so remove altogether odhf_valid <- odhf_data survey_sf <- odhf_valid %>% st_as_sf(coords=c("long", "lat"), crs=st_crs(4326)) %>% select(-facility_name) %>% st_transform(st_crs(flood_data)) 4.3 Compute Intersections The following code loops through each hospital to determine flood exposure for the 24 months leading up to the month the survey was conducted at each location. We will use a 25km buffer to encapsulate floods that occurred in areas near to the hospitals. buffer_distance = 25000 #in metres #create a buffer around each poi survey_buffered <- st_buffer(survey_sf, dist = buffer_distance) #find floods within each poi's buffer flood_matches <- st_intersects(survey_buffered, flood_data) #extract year and month from flood event datetime flood_data <- flood_data %>% mutate(flood_year = year(datetime_utc), flood_month = month(datetime_utc)) #initialize an empty data frame to store results exposure_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(survey_sf), ncol = 25) colnames(exposure_matrix) <- paste0("month_", 0:24) #column names for each month #loop through each poi and determine flood exposure for (i in seq_len(nrow(survey_sf))) { #extract the survey date from the survey related columns survey_year <- survey_sf$survey_year[i] survey_month <- survey_sf$survey_month[i] #compute the 24-month range month_seq <- seq.Date(from = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", survey_year, survey_month)) %m-% months(1), length.out = 24, by = "-1 month") month_seq_df <- data.frame(year = year(month_seq), month = month(month_seq)) #get the indices of intersecting floods for this poi flood_indices <- flood_matches[[i]] if (length(flood_indices) > 0) { #if floods exist within the buffer flood_events <- flood_data[flood_indices, c("flood_year", "flood_month")] #check for each of the past 24 months if a flood occurred for (j in 1:24) { target_year <- month_seq_df$year[j] target_month <- month_seq_df$month[j] #if a flood occurred in this year-month, set exposure to 1 if (any(flood_events$flood_year == target_year & flood_events$flood_month == target_month)) { exposure_matrix[i, j] <- 1 } } } } #convert matrix to a data frame and merge with survey data exposure_df <- as.data.frame(exposure_matrix) #bind to the presence absence matrix survey_floods_pa <- cbind(survey_sf, exposure_df) #summarise based on the number of unique hospitals survey_floods_pa %>% summarise(n_unique = n_distinct(hospital_id)) #create a summary dataset of hospitals with only flood events for easier viewing survey_floods_pa_filtered <- survey_floods_pa %>% filter(if_any(starts_with("month_"), ~ . == 1)) #write to a directory write.csv(survey_floods_pa, r"(./data/flood_presence_absence.csv)") Display a snippet of the floods matrix. #print a selection of data kable(head(survey_floods_pa_filtered),'html') %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>% scroll_box(height = "300px") odhf_facility_type hospital_id postalcode Below is a visual depiction of flooding events in the area adjacent to the hospital. floods_summary_matrix <- read.csv(r"(./data/flood_presence_absence.csv)", row.names=1) survey_sf$hospital_id <- as.character(survey_sf$hospital_id) floods_summary_matrix$hospital_id <- as.character(floods_summary_matrix$hospital_id) #South Okanagan General Hospital floods_summary_map <- floods_summary_matrix %>% left_join(survey_sf %>% select(hospital_id, geometry), by = "hospital_id") #get the associated floods hospital_509 <- survey_floods_pa %>% filter(hospital_id == 509) #get the intersecting floods flood_509 <- st_intersection(st_buffer(hospital_509, dist = buffer_distance), flood_data) #generate the map elements mapview( flood_509, layer.name = "Intersecting Floods", popup = leafpop::popupTable( flood_509, zcol = c("swath_id", "product_file_name") ) ) + mapview( filter(survey_sf, hospital_id == 509), col.regions = "red", cex = 6, layer.name = "Hospital Location" ) + mapview( st_buffer(filter(survey_sf, hospital_id == 509), buffer_distance), col.regions = "green", alpha.regions = 0.1, layer.name = "Hospital Buffer (25km)" )

6 Heat Huge swings in temperature are becoming more and more common when comparing seasonal highs and lows. It is much harder to stay cool in heat… 6.1 Environmental Data Preparation Our first step is to load and transform the hospital data. Temperature data was sourced from the weathercan R package. #load the data odhf_valid <- read.csv("./data/odhf_hospitals.csv", row.names = 1) survey_sf <- odhf_valid %>% st_as_sf(coords=c("long", "lat"), crs=st_crs(4326)) %>% select(-facility_name) survey_sf <- st_transform(survey_sf, 3978) stations_list <- stations() names(stations_list) In order to collect the relevant weather stations and time frames, the minimum and maximum survey data collection periods needed to be collected from the ODHF data. #identify the date range survey_sf <- survey_sf %>% mutate( weather_start = make_date(survey_year - 2, survey_month, 1), #Start date: 2 years before weather_end = make_date(survey_year, survey_month, days_in_month(make_date(survey_year, survey_month, 1)))) min_start_year <- min(year(survey_sf$weather_start), na.rm = TRUE) max_end_year <- max(year(survey_sf$weather_end), na.rm = TRUE) stations_by_day <- filter(stations_list, interval %in% c("hour","day"), #setting the min coverage years for data at the stations #is to increase likelihood that the same hospital location will be assigned to the same weather station #across survey years #this will reduce noise introduced as a result of pulling data for the same location from different sources #which may have different data available, different frequencies of collection, etc. start <= min_start_year, end >= max_end_year) Next, we need to get the nearest distance to stations for evaluation of if they are too close or too far away. In the case of this example, no station will be too far away. #get the stations by day stations_by_day_sf <- st_as_sf(stations_by_day, coords=c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) stations_by_day_sf <- st_transform(stations_by_day_sf, st_crs(survey_sf)) #get the nearest feature nearest_stations <- st_nearest_feature(survey_sf, stations_by_day_sf) #get the nearest distances and ids of the stations for each hospital survey_sf$nearest_dist <- st_distance(survey_sf, stations_by_day_sf[nearest_stations,], by_element = TRUE) survey_sf$near_station_id <- stations_by_day_sf[nearest_stations,]$station_id survey_sf$station_interval <- stations_by_day_sf[nearest_stations,]$interval survey_sf <- survey_sf %>% rename(station_id=near_station_id) Here, we get the data from the weathercan package. #query the package for every station that was identified hourly_station_ids <- filter(survey_sf, station_interval == "hour") %>% pull(station_id) daily_station_ids <- filter(survey_sf, station_interval == "day") %>% pull(station_id) daily_weather <- weather_dl(station_ids = daily_station_ids, start=min(survey_sf$weather_start), end=max(survey_sf$weather_end), interval='day') hourly_weather <- weather_dl(station_ids = hourly_station_ids, start=min(survey_sf$weather_start), end=max(survey_sf$weather_end), interval='hour') Then, we group and combine the hourly with the daily so a comprehensive dataset is created. #summarize from hourly to daily and combine hourly_as_daily_weather_original <- hourly_weather %>% group_by(station_id, date, lat, lon) %>% summarise( min_temp = min(temp, na.rm = FALSE), max_temp = max(temp, na.rm = FALSE), .groups = "drop" ) hourly_as_daily_weather <- subset(hourly_as_daily_weather_original, select = -c(lat, lon)) combined_hourly_daily <- bind_rows(hourly_as_daily_weather, daily_weather) %>% select(any_of(intersect(names(hourly_as_daily_weather), names(daily_weather)))) write_parquet(combined_hourly_daily, r"(./data/odhf_weather_stations.parquet)") 6.2 Heat ECCC Environment and Climate Change Canada has their own criteria for extreme heat events around the country. Using a rough sketch of the criteria map, we can relate the hospital data to the temperature data. combined_hourly_daily <- read_parquet(r"(./data/odhf_weather_stations.parquet)") eccc_friendly <- st_read(r"(./data/roughEcccMap_final.gpkg)") survey_sf_eccc <- st_join(survey_sf, eccc_friendly) consecutive_days <- 2 #2 days and nights as the criteria. #identify days of consecutive heat heat_flagged_eccc <- survey_sf_eccc %>% left_join(combined_hourly_daily, by='station_id') %>% #date, station_id, max_temp, min_temp unique(.,by=c("hospital_id", "survey_month", "survey_year", "date")) %>% #get unique entries based on survey_id, survey month + year, and date of station data collection arrange(station_id, date) %>% #need dates in order chronologically group_by(station_id, hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year) %>% #station_ids grouped together mutate( hot = max_temp >= day_thresh & min_temp >= nite_thres, #if the max_temp is greater than the day threshold AND the minimum temperature is greater than the nighttime threshold run_id = rleid(hot) #add unique id for runs ) %>% group_by(hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year, station_id, run_id) %>% #group by station id and the run ids (looking for two or more) mutate( run_len = sum(hot), #sum the number of hot events per run heat_event = hot & run_len >= consecutive_days #only classed as a heat event if two or more days ) %>% ungroup() %>% select(-run_id, -run_len) %>% mutate(date = as.Date(date)) 6.2.1 Date Lag As part of the exposure determination, we are interested in the 24 months prior to each survey date at the hospitals. Hospitals were surveyed at different times, so the date of the survey will be recorded along with each month from the 0th to 24th month prior (survey month, survey month - 1, survey month - 2, etc.). expand_months <- function(d, hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year, station_id) { data.table( hospital_id = hospital_id, survey_year = survey_year, survey_month = survey_month, station_id = station_id, offset = 0:24, date = format(ceiling_date(d %m-% months(0:24), "month") - days(1), "%Y%m") ) } #apply the function #identifies how many months a given month is offset from the 0th month for that surveys survey date survey_sf$dates <- ymd(paste(survey_sf$survey_year, survey_sf$survey_month, "01", sep = "-")) + months(1) - days(1) #FOR EVERY UNIQUE survey AND SURVEY DATE COMBINATION <- this is key surveys_un <- unique(survey_sf, by = c("survey_id","dates")) surveys_un <- as.data.table(surveys_un) survey_expanded <- surveys_un[, expand_months(dates, hospital_id, survey_month, 7 PM 2.5 7.1 Environmental Data Preparation This data is just for checking! odhf_pm25 <- read.csv("./data/odhf_hospitals.csv", row.names = 1) %>% mutate( pm25_start = make_date(survey_year - 2, survey_month, 1), #start 2 years before pm25_end = make_date(survey_year, survey_month, days_in_month(make_date(survey_year, survey_month, 1)))) #last day of the month head(odhf_pm25) #define years years <- 2015:2018 #define the base path base_path <- "./data/pm25/" #read, standardize, and pivot dataset load_pm25_data <- function(year) { suffix <- substr(as.character(year), 3, 4) #get just the year from the year range file <- file.path(base_path, paste0("aqsmk_avc_", suffix, ".csv")) #the base path of the files + the year df <- read_csv(file, show_col_types = FALSE) names(df)[1] <- "postalcode" df_long <- df %>% #pivot the data to long format based on the columns in the data pivot_longer( cols = starts_with("aqsmk"), #column for the aqsmk data names_to = "var", values_to = "pm25" ) %>% mutate( ym_raw = str_extract(var, "\\d{2}_\\d{2}"), #regex year = 2000 + as.integer(substr(ym_raw, 1, 2)), month = as.integer(substr(ym_raw, 4, 5)) #all data points are january ) %>% select(postalcode, province, year, month, pm25) %>% filter(!is.na(pm25)) %>% rename(postcode=postalcode) df_long } pm25_all_years <- map_dfr(years, load_pm25_data) #load all the csvs # #turn month into a factor with correct order #pm25_all_years <- pm25_all_years %>% # mutate(month = factor(month, levels = c("jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun", # "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"))) #rename for later actions pm25_all_years <- pm25_all_years %>% rename(survey_year=year) %>% rename(survey_month=month) 7.2 Date Lag {pm25-date-lag} Lag the data in the same way as the other datasets. expand_months <- function(d, hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year, postalcode) { data.table( hospital_id = hospital_id, survey_year = survey_year, survey_month = survey_month, postcode = postalcode, offset = 0:24, date = format(ceiling_date(d %m-% months(0:24), "month") - days(1), "%Y%m") ) } #apply the function #identifies how many months a given month is offset from the 0th month for that surveys survey date odhf_pm25$dates <- ymd(paste(odhf_pm25$survey_year, odhf_pm25$survey_month, "01", sep = "-")) + months(1) - days(1) #FOR EVERY UNIQUE survey AND SURVEY DATE COMBINATION <- this is key surveys_un <- unique(odhf_pm25, by = c("survey_id","dates")) surveys_un <- as.data.table(surveys_un) survey_expanded <- surveys_un[, expand_months(dates, hospital_id, survey_month, survey_year, postalcode), by = .(hospital_id, dates)] survey_expanded <- survey_expanded %>% select(-3) survey_expanded_pm25 <- survey_expanded %>% rename(year_month = date) 7.3 Data Manipulation {pm25-data-manipulation} Create a summary matrix of all the PM2.5 values for the months. 8 Appendix 8.1 Survey Data Generation #generation of data based on entries in the hospital data #if there are 20 hospitals, make 20 random months for survey between 1 and 12 and random years choosing between 2016 and 2020 #https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/pub/13-26-0001/2020001/ODHF_v1.1.zip #make sure the latitude and longitude columns exist and that there is an id column as well #set a random seed set.seed(933) #read in the raw data odhf <- read.csv("./data/odhf_v1.1.csv") #create an id list odhf$hospital_id <- 1:nrow(odhf) #can only use valid lat/long locations odhf_valid <- odhf[!is.na(odhf[["latitude"]]) & !is.na(odhf[["longitude"]]), ] odhf_valid <- odhf_valid %>% filter(odhf_facility_type=="Hospitals") %>% select(c("latitude", "longitude", "facility_name", "odhf_facility_type", "hospital_id", "postal_code")) #strip spaces from postal code odhf_valid$postal_code <- gsub(" ", "", odhf_valid$postal_code) odhf_valid <- odhf_valid %>% rename(postalcode = postal_code) #randomization odhf_valid[[survey_month_col]] <- sample(1:12, size = nrow(odhf_valid), replace = TRUE) odhf_valid[[survey_year_col]] <- sample(2018:2021, size=nrow(odhf_valid), replace = TRUE) #change names setnames(odhf_valid, c("latitude", "longitude"), c("lat","long")) #write for reading in elsewhere write.csv(odhf_valid, "./data/odhf_hospitals.csv")
